sentences: In a dim room, the tax collector Matthew sits at a table with his companions, counting money.
Through a doorway on the right, Christ enters and stretches out his hand to point at him.
That hand echoes Adam's in Michelangelo's Creation of Adam, hinting that a new creation is beginning.
Light falls from above Christ's head in a sharp diagonal, catching the faces at the table one by one.
A bearded man points to his own chest as if to ask "Me?"
, and he is usually taken to be Matthew, though some argue Matthew is the young man hunched over his coins at the end of the table.
Everyone wears the clothes of Caravaggio's own day, so the Bible story seems to happen in a Roman back street.
It was his first public commission, and it still hangs in the chapel it was painted for.
